[SOURCE id=issue:573:573-summary:f08f497b1daa kind=issue issue=573 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#573.txt]
Issue: 573
Summary: On OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf, the unconnected explicit TCP `SendRRData` path has a remotely reachable out-of-bounds read. `CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure()` recognizes optional sockaddr info items (`0x8000` / `0x8001`) and then reads the remaining fixed sockaddr fields without first checking that those bytes are still inside the received CPF buffer. The observed failure occurs before `NotifyMessageRouter()`, with the first invalid access in `GetIntFromMessage()`; ASan reports it as a stack-buffer-overflow crossing the right boundary of `incoming_message[512]` in `HandleDataOnTcpSocket()`.
Reproduce: Tested against OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf. The PoC is a Python 3 script that connects to TCP port 44818 on `OPENER_HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`), first sends a `RegisterSession` request (`0x0065`) and then a `SendRRData` request (`0x006F`). Run the script in `baseline` mode to send a normal CPF with a Null Address Item and an Unconnected Data Item, or in `crash` mode to send a 482-byte CPF whose last two bytes are `0x8000` so the packet ends with a recognized sockaddr info item. The crash case is: item count 3, Null Address Item, Unconnected Data Item length 470 filled with `A`, then trailing `0x8000`. Expected result: the target crashes before `NotifyMessageRouter()` is entered; the first invalid access is in `GetIntFromMessage()`, and ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow on `incoming_message[512]` in `HandleDataOnTcpSocket()`.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:572:572-summary:4cac5b77f97f kind=issue issue=572 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#572.txt]
Issue: 572
Summary: In OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf, the real TCP explicit-message path on port 44818 (`RegisterSession` / `SendRRData`) can reach `SetAttributeList()` with a default-registered, non-settable `kCipShortString` attribute: Identity class, instance 1, attribute 7 (`product_name`). For non-settable attributes, `SetAttributeList()` still advances over the attacker-supplied value, and for variable-length types it calls `GetCipDataTypeLength(attribute->type, message_router_request->data)` without validating remaining length. For `kCipShortString`, that leads to an unchecked 1-byte read via `GetSintFromMessage()`. With a long padded EPath positioning `message_router_request->data` at the end of the 512-byte stack receive buffer, ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read. The document states this is at minimum a remote unauthenticated denial of service in the default build.
Reproduce: Use OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf with the default Ethernet buffer size (`PC_OPENER_ETHERNET_BUFFER_SIZE=512`). Start the server, then run the provided Python 3 PoC in `crash` mode against TCP port 44818 (default host `127.0.0.1`, override with `OPENER_HOST`). The script first sends `RegisterSession`, then `SendRRData` carrying a CIP `SetAttributeList` request to Identity class 1, instance 1, attribute 7. In crash mode it builds a long padded EPath (`build_path(233)`) and sends `attr_count=1`, `attr=7`, with no short-string length byte following the attribute id. Expected result: ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read when `SetAttributeList()` skips the non-settable short string value.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:570:570-summary:0b4cbe808107 kind=issue issue=570 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#570.txt]
Issue: 570
Summary: A malformed `ForwardOpen` request can trigger a network-reachable out-of-bounds read in OpENer during connection-path parsing. In `ParseConnectionPath()`, the trailing Simple Data Segment length byte is trusted without checking that it still fits the remaining path budget, so `remaining_path` can underflow and `message` can be advanced past the request buffer. The next `GetPathSegmentType(message)` access then reads out of bounds and crashes the server. The reachable path shown is `HandleDataOnTcpSocket()` -> `HandleReceivedExplictTcpData()` -> `HandleReceivedSendRequestResponseDataCommand()` -> `NotifyCommonPacketFormat()` -> `NotifyMessageRouter()` -> `NotifyClass()` -> `ForwardOpen()` -> `ForwardOpenRoutine()` -> `HandleNonNullNonMatchingForwardOpenRequest()` -> `ParseConnectionPath()` -> `GetPathSegmentType()`. `HandleNonNullNonMatchingForwardOpenRequest()` calls `ParseConnectionPath()` before any `open_connection_function` is called.
Reproduce: Run the provided Python 3 PoC against an OpENer server listening on `127.0.0.1:44818`. The script registers a session, wraps a CIP `ForwardOpen` request to Connection Manager class `0x06`, instance `1`, inside `SendRRData`, and sends it over TCP 44818. It supports `baseline` and `crash`; `baseline` uses the valid path `20 04 24 97 2C 96 2C 64`, while `crash` appends `80 FF` so the trailing Simple Data Segment claims `0xff` words with only one word left. Command: `python3 poc.py crash`. On the vulnerable server, `ParseConnectionPath()` underflows `remaining_path`, advances past the request buffer, and `GetPathSegmentType()` dereferences out of bounds and crashes the server.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:582:582-summary:a17fd2adbb9f kind=issue issue=582 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#582.txt]
Issue: 582
Summary: OpENer 2.3.0 (commit 76b95cf) has an out-of-bounds read in CIP message parsing when handling malformed explicit requests with a forged EPath size. An ENIP SendRRData request can carry a very short CIP payload whose attacker-controlled path_size claims more path words than are actually available; because the parser continues decoding path segments without a remaining-length boundary, it reads past the end of the stack receive buffer. The report states this is remotely triggerable via network traffic and does not require authentication.
Reproduce: Use the provided Python 3 PoC against a target listening on 127.0.0.1:44818 by default (defaults: attempts=1, timeout=1.5, interval_ms=0, path_words=240, buffer_size=512). The client opens a TCP connection, sends ENIP RegisterSession (0x0065) with payload <HH>(1,0), and extracts the returned session ID. It then sends ENIP SendRRData (0x006F) for that session with 6 zero command-specific bytes plus a CPF whose item count is 3, containing a Null Address item (0x0000, length 0) and an Unconnected Data item (0x00B2) whose declared data length is only 2 bytes: service 0x0E followed by a forged path_size byte set to the requested path_words value. The PoC then appends repeated 0x20 0x01 bytes after that declared payload until the whole packet reaches 512 bytes, sends it, and waits for a reply. Reported outcomes are either RESP - response_len=... or FAIL - no response (reset, crash, or ASan abort), or an exception.
[/SOURCE]
